title: Borderlands Scrapped Its Art Style Less Than a Year Before Launch
hook: In 2008 Gearbox was about 75 percent done with Borderlands when testers said it looked like Fallout 3, so it redrew the whole game in a hand-drawn style with months to spare. This week the series passed 100 million copies sold. Would you have played the gritty brown version?
script: Did you know Borderlands threw out its entire art style less than a year before launch? When Game Informer revealed the game on its cover in September of two thousand seven, it looked grim and realistic. The pitch was Diablo meets Mad Max, with the same dark, gritty graphics as every other shooter of the time. By October of 2008, Gearbox knew it had a problem. Testers said the game looked too much like Fallout 3, which had just come out. The studio also feared being seen as a poor man's Rage, the shooter id Software was building. Borderlands was about three quarters finished at that point. Gearbox decided to be remarkable rather than invisible, and started over on the look. The team switched to a hand drawn, illustrated style that matched the wild guns and humor. The new look went public in April of 2009, barely six months before release. The game launched on consoles on October 20, 2009. By that December, Take-Two said it had sold more than two million copies. The gamble paid off for a long time. This week Gearbox announced the Borderlands series has now passed one hundred million units sold. Would the brown version have made it this far? Follow for more gaming history.
